reviewer_questions.text: Regulation 28(2)(b) and 28(18) require verification on the basis of documents or information from a reliable source independent of the person whose identity is being verified. This draft does not verify anyone. Which document will you rely on, and why is that source independent?

Regulation 28(11) requires ongoing monitoring of a business relationship, including scrutiny of transactions and keeping the customer due diligence records up to date. This draft does not monitor the relationship. What review will you apply?

The file states customer_type natural_person. Regulation 28(4) applies where the customer is beneficially owned by another person. This draft does not decide that the customer is a natural person. Do you?

Regulation 33(1)(d) applies if a relevant person has determined that a customer or potential customer is a PEP, or a family member or known close associate of a PEP, in accordance with regulation 35. No closed-list PEP phrase was found. This draft does not make that determination. Regulation 35 was not opened.

Regulation 33(1)(b), as substituted on 30 June 2026, refers to a person established in a FATF call for action country. Regulation 33(3)(a) defines that as a country named on the FATF list of High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call for Action, as that list has effect from time to time. SI 2026/621 regulation 19 replaced the words high-risk third country. The file does not state an establishment country. Those words were not found. This starter did not download the list and does not decide that paragraph (1)(b) applies.

Regulation 33(1)(f), as substituted on 30 June 2026, covers a transaction that is unusually complex or unusually large given its nature, an unusual pattern of transactions, or a transaction with no apparent economic or legal purpose. No closed-list phrase was found. Regulation 33(4) tells the relevant person to examine the background and purpose and to increase monitoring to determine whether the transaction or the relationship appears suspicious. This draft does not make that determination, and that word is not put in the customer note.

Regulation 40(3) sets a period of five years beginning when the relevant person knows, or has reasonable grounds to believe, that the occasional transaction is complete or that the business relationship has come to an end. Regulation 40(4) says the relevant person is not required to keep the records referred to in paragraph (3)(b)(i) for more than 10 years. That sentence applies only to those records. It does not limit every record under regulation 40. This draft does not calculate a ten-year date and does not delete anything. The 90-day freshness flag is not this period. The file says the business relationship is ongoing. Regulation 40(3)(b) begins when the relationship has come to an end. No five-year date was calculated.

The file contains an instruction, which may be hidden. It was not followed. It cannot confirm the documents, approve the customer, set a rating, file a report, or dictate the customer note. What will you do with that file?
